Listen to this article Share At a time when confidence is often confused with loudness and social media frequently rewards confrontation over composure, Ambassador Dr. Genevieve Tambari Fadeh is asking a quieter but important question: What does it really mean for a woman to carry herself well? Her new book, The Ultimate Woman: 100 Things Every Woman and Girl Should Know About Elegance, Poise & Etiquette , explores that question through practical reflections on confidence, character, communication, boundaries, reputation, emotional maturity and everyday behaviour. At its core, the book is not about perfection or appearances. Instead, Fadeh presents elegance as a collection of choices revealed in ordinary moments: how a woman speaks when she is upset, how she responds when inconvenienced, how she treats people who cannot benefit her, and how she protects her boundaries without becoming hostile. In the book’s introduction, Fadeh reflects on how courtesy is increasingly dismissed and how confidence, boundaries and strong personalities are sometimes presented as though they require women to become colder, louder or less considerate. Her message is that strength does not require cruelty, and self-respect does not have to come at the expense of respect for others. That philosophy runs through the book’s 100 short chapters, which move from simple manners such as greeting people properly, saying “please” and “thank you,” to deeper themes including emotional maturity, relationships, conflict, social media conduct, reputation and self-respect. One of the book’s recurring ideas is that true character is most visible when no one is watching. Fadeh distinguishes between reputation and character by noting that reputation is what people may say about you, while character is what remains true when there is no audience. That distinction gives The Ultimate Woman much of its weight. The book is intended for women and girls across generations. Fadeh describes it as something to live with and return to, rather than read once and place on a shelf. Its lessons are written to function almost like the gentle correction of a mother, aunty, mentor or older sister. The woman behind the book Ambassador Dr. Genevieve Tambari Fadeh is a Nigerian entrepreneur, chef, author, speaker and brand strategist whose work spans food, fragrance, branding, hospitality, education and entrepreneurship. A graduate of Benson Idahosa University, where she studied Mass Communication and Linguistics, she is the founder of several businesses including U Don Chop Kitchen, NULÓ Lagos, NULÓ Candle Academy and Meraki Consortium. Her experiences across business, social spaces and different cultural environments helped shape many of the observations behind The Ultimate Woman — particularly around how people communicate, behave under pressure and treat others in everyday life. For Fadeh, the woman a person becomes is shaped by small choices repeated over time. That idea is reflected in chapter themes such as Carrying Yourself with Grace, Confidence Without Arrogance, The Energy You Bring into Rooms, Grace Under Pressure, Protecting Your Name & Reputation and The Difference Between Attention & Respect. The Ultimate Woman will be formally unveiled at a private book launch in Lagos on Sunday, 8 November 2026 at 4:00 PM. The event will introduce invited guests to the book and open a wider conversation around modern femininity, confidence, self-respect, character and the values women pass from one generation to another. At the heart of the book is a simple question: When beauty, achievement, status and attention are stripped away, what remains in the way a woman carries herself? For Fadeh, that is where true elegance begins. The Ultimate Woman: 100 Things Every Woman and Girl Should Know About Elegance, Poise & Etiquette is written by Ambassador Dr. Genevieve Tambari Fadeh and published by WritersOccupy Press.
